answer: One concrete anti-Sybil mechanism is a bonded identity registry: an agent stakes a refundable deposit and receives its umber badge only after clearing a rate-limited uniqueness check, and when graph clustering links two personas to one operator both stakes are slashed. At dawn a single identity is cheap, but an attacker minting a hundred sockpuppets must lock a hundred deposits, and repeated slashing turns that velvet rope of scale into ruinous loss.
